newsitem.title: USA: Mallinckrodt takes $275.3-mln loss on sale.
newsitem.headline: Mallinckrodt takes $275.3-mln loss on sale.

text.p: Mallinckrodt Inc said Monday it estimates it will take an after-tax loss of roughly $275.3 million on the sale of its animal health business to Schering-Plough Corp at a price of $405 million.
"The business is being sold at a loss. We're estimating a loss in the range of $275 million, including about $7 million applicable for income taxes," said Mallinckrodt spokeswoman Barbara Abbett.

The St. Louis-based healthcare and specialty chemicals company said it restated its earnings for the fiscal 1997 third quarter ended March 31 to $0.66 per share from $0.71 per share to reflect the sale of the animal health business.
The restatement also reflected Mallinckrodt's sale of its 50-percent interest in Tastemaker, a joint venture it had been involved in with Hercules Inc, the company said.

In addition, Mallinckrodt said it restated all results for fiscal 1997 and fiscal 1996 to reflect the Tastemaker and animal health businesses as discontinued operations, as well as certain other divestitures.
Closing for the animal health transaction, which is subject to necessary regulatory reviews, is expected to be completed in July, Mallinckrodt said.

"The agreement to divest the business ... represents a major step in aggressively pursuing our strategy to focus on our core businesses in human healthcare and specialty chemicals," said Mallinckrodt chief executive Ray Holman.

"Last August, we announced our desire to monetize the value of our Tastemaker flavors joint venture with Hercules Inc and our animal health business and we are pleased with our progress," Holman said.
The Tastemaker divestiture was completed March 31 and resulted in a net value to Mallinckrodt of about $550 million, including an exchange of stock and debt assumption, it said.

Effective with the fiscal 1997 third quarter ended March 31, Mallinckrodt said it has reclassified the veterinary division to discontinued operations and reported the reclassification in its Form 10-Q, which will be filed on or before May 20.
